doc.title: Michi Fuji interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: First hearing jazz: Coltrane, Miles and Grappelli
summary: At 14 or 15 she bought Coltrane CDs without understanding them, then heard Miles Davis and Stephane Grappelli, whose tone and swing she likes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Okay. Do you remember your first exposure to jazz music — hearing jazz for the first time?

Yeah. I was I think 15 or 14 years old. I was buying the Coltrane album but I totally did not understand that music. But I was buying the CD’s. And also I was going to the library and checking out some jazz music. Yeah. It was like 14, a teenager. But I no understand, just listening.
But you don’t have to understand it to like it.
Of course when you pick out Coltrane too, that could be a little overwhelming.
Yeah. Maybe the cover of the CD is cool. I don’t know.
Sure. You’re attracted by the look of it.
So you didn’t listen to violin players first?
In jazz, later, yeah. For jazz I was listening at that time to Coltrane and Miles. Miles Davis. And then, oh I heard Stephane Grappelli. I tried to listen to that.
Did you like that era of music? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-
Yeah. I like Stephane Grappelli, and his tone and swing and his music.
